Addendum: I am putting this at the top as I wish people to see it first. Before you down-vote me as a knee jerk reaction, please take the time to actually read what I have to say, and the posts after. I am not for traditional gun control, I am not a liberal trying to take guns, In fact I am pro 2nd amendment. So please, respectfully take the time to be productive and mature instead of a typical negative reaction to the subject, rather than taking part in a reasonable discussion. Thanks!

Now back to my initial post:

Interesting perspective in that it calls for more active positive work with identified likely subjects that would cause issues.

I could be wrong, but in the majority of mass shootings the aggressors do not have a prior criminal history?

This is great, however for lowering gun violence in the criminal class.

I have always advocated vesting the person, not limiting the guns.

In other words, having to prove you can be a responsible gun owner before getting a licence to own one.

I thought it would be better to have a mandatory gun class, set over a week time, with instructors who have been vetted to look for people who may be an issue (anger, mentally ill, etc.) in addition to background checks, etc. And one must prove they can store the weapon properly (gun safe of the like) so that access to the gun is limited. Careers where a gun is needed, military/police, etc. could substitute their official training for this same thing.

The instructor then could fail you for any reason, without telling the person why. They would then have to have to wait, say six months or so, before trying again. As long as one owns the gun, one would have to do this every 2 years.

At that point, I really don't care much what small arms the individual has, as the person is vetted to be safe, not the weapon.

I would also like to see more a push for technology that will only allow the weapon to be fired by the owner. Maybe fingerprint, or something similar.

With the fingerprint technology in your solution, could you set it to recognize multiple finger prints? Also, would their be more than one finger able to activate in case of a broken or cut or burned finger? Would the government or any other agency be able to turn off said technology to render guns useless? Would this cover hunting guns as well? As it is you have to pass a safety course in all states to get a hunting permit which covers a lot of what you outlined in your statement. Would you be able to skip said hunting course since you would have already taken a safety course?

I think you bring up a lot of great points. So lets go through them:

could you set it to recognize multiple finger prints?

I would have to say for this part, to be effective, it could only be set for fingerprints from a person who has already been vetted, but not changed by the owner directly. Also, would their be more than one finger able to activate in case of a broken or cut or burned finger?
